cards.text: Friend, it's feast time, and people have come up to worship. Some of them are Greeks. They walk right up to Philip, one of Jesus' disciples, who's from Bethsaida in Galilee.

cards.question: The Greeks at the feast have one request for Philip. What do they want?

answers.text: To find a place to stay

cards.text: Philip doesn't take it straight to Jesus. He passes the Greeks' request along to Andrew, another of Jesus' disciples.

cards.question: Next, Philip and Andrew go to Jesus together to tell Him about the Greeks' request. True or false?

cards.text: Two disciples, one request. That's every question at work that gets passed from one desk to the NEXT desk before it ever lands with the person who can answer it.
Jesus replies, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

cards.question: Next Jesus gives a picture of a kernel of wheat falling to the ground. What does He say has to happen to it for it to bear much fruit?

cards.text: Unless the kernel dies, it remains only a seed. Same in my bakery, friend: dough that never goes in the oven stays DOUGH, and you can stare at that bowl all week for a cookie count of ZERO.

cards.question: Jesus turns from the seed to people. He says whoever loves his life will keep it. True or false?

cards.text: Flipped: whoever loves his life will lose it, but whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life. Then Jesus talks about anyone who serves Him.

cards.question: Jesus says anyone who serves Him must ___ Him, and where He is, His servant will be as well.
Jesus says anyone who serves Him will be honored. Who does Jesus say will give that honor?
Now that the hour has come, Jesus says something about His own soul. How does He say His soul is now?
Jesus wonders whether He should ask the Father to save Him from this hour. Then He asks the Father for exactly that. True or false?

cards.text: Instead, Jesus says it is for this purpose that He has come to this hour. Then He says, “Father, glorify Your name!”

cards.question: Jesus has just asked the Father to glorify His name. What happens right after?

cards.text: The voice says, “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.” Out loud. From HEAVEN.
So a voice just came from heaven, and the crowd standing there heard it. But they don't all say the same thing about it.

cards.question: Some in the crowd say it had thundered. Others say ___ had spoken to Jesus.

cards.text: Some say thunder, some say angel, and that's every office after a loud bang down the hall: one person says “just the printer,” and the other one is ALREADY out of their chair to go look. Then Jesus speaks up.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd the voice from heaven came for His benefit, not theirs. True or false?

cards.text: The voice was for them. Then Jesus says, “Now judgment is upon this world; now the prince of this world will be cast out.”

cards.question: Next Jesus talks about being lifted up from the earth. When He is, what does He say He will do?
The writer explains that Jesus spoke of being lifted up to indicate the kind of death He was going to die. True or false?

cards.text: The crowd pushes back. They've heard from the Law that the Christ, the Messiah (John 1:41), will remain forever, so how can Jesus say the Son of Man must be lifted up?

cards.question: The crowd can't make the Law and Jesus' words about being lifted up fit together. What else do they ask Him?

answers.text: Who this Son of Man is
Where He plans to go next

cards.text: Big question, friend. Then Jesus tells them, “For a little while longer, the Light will be among you.”

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd to walk while they have the Light, so that ___ will not overtake them.

cards.text: Jesus says, “The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.” Every adult alive has walked through the house at night with the lights off and found the corner of the couch with their pinky toe.

cards.question: While the crowd still has the Light, Jesus tells them to wait for it to come back later. True or false?
Jesus tells the crowd to believe while there's still time. If they do, what does He say they may become?
After Jesus has spoken these things to the crowd, what does He do?

answers.text: He goes away and is hidden from them
He stays and heals the sick among them
He goes up to teach in the temple
